$comment: Named benchmark sets: a fixed list of matches, so two revisions are measured on the same
thing. A round that says 'this won 4 of 5 on smoke against the control's 1 of 5' has made a
comparison; a round that says 'we lost again' on a random map, a random faction and a random
seed has made an anecdote, because faction, map and opponent all moved at once.
Seeds are arbitrary constants. Their only job is to be the same next time, so do not change
one to chase a nicer number - that silently invalidates every stored result for the set.
Add a new set instead. Factions are pinned for the same reason: consecutive rounds that
played GDI then Nod were comparing two different games.

sets.name: smoke
sets.summary: Five matches, both factions, one map. The quickest thing that is still a measurement.

sets.name: standard
sets.summary: Two maps by both factions by three seeds. The set to quote in a round's result.
